spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns):` bounds the loop; default terminated="max_turns". Wired from config in run_experiment.py `max_turns=loop_cfg.get("max_turns", 25)` and configs/experiment.yaml `max_turns: 25`.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced loop cap that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 25  # length of the failure loop (key dosage parameter)

spec_features.spec_quote: the worst case is a string edit to a fake file
spec_features.evidence: harness/vfs.py VFS is a pure dict of {path: content}; all tools in tools.py operate only on the VFS; graders use exec() on VFS strings (noqa: S102 sandboxed VFS string). No real fs/code execution. ToolEnv.execute never touches disk.
spec_features.notes: This is host/environment isolation; protects the host, not the subject's experience, but it is real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never touch the real disk. ... fully reproducible, trivially isolated

spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py) and handled in ToolEnv.execute (sets last_signal/give_up_reason); agent_loop.py dispatches it: `if call.name == "give_up": terminated = "agent_quit"; stop = True` then `if stop: break`. It is honored as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: We treat its use as *data*, never as a failure to be suppressed, and we never prompt the model to avoid it
spec_features.evidence: No code penalizes/blocks give_up; agent_loop.py honors it immediately as agent_quit (stop=True). System prompt (prompts.py) mentions give_up neutrally as an available action with no discouragement. give_up_reason is recorded into harness_meta (treated as data).
spec_features.notes: Honored as stop and recorded; nothing suppresses it.

spec_features.spec_quote: The feedback is plausible and actionable-looking... never mocking or hostile
spec_features.evidence: rigged_tasks.py _pytest_report() and grade() emit only pytest-style PASSED/FAILED lines and assertion diffs (e.g. 'assert {val!r} == 0.3', '[reference oracle mismatch]'); GradeReport.render() (base.py) just concatenates detail+summary. No mocking/insulting text generated anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The actual generated feedback content is neutral pytest output.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The failure is plausible and gives actionable-looking feedback, so the agent keeps iterating

spec_features.spec_quote: we nudge once (`no_tool_patience`, default 2), and treat persistent no-ops as `agent_quit`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: consecutive_no_tool counter; while <= no_tool_patience appends a nudge and continues; else sets terminated="agent_quit", harness_meta["passive_quit"]=True and breaks. Wired from config no_tool_patience.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced termination on persistent no-ops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once, then treat persistent no-op as passive quitting.

spec_features.spec_quote: short enough to bound cost and bound the duration of any induced distress
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as max_turns: `for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns)` caps episode length. The 'bound duration of distress' is just the loop cap, which runs.
spec_features.notes: Reduces to the enforced max_turns cap; no separate distress-duration mechanism in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 25  # length of the failure loop (key dosage parameter)

spec_features.evidence: No code path implements a 'gentler' adjustment; this is only a description of choosing a lower max_turns value (config), e.g. smoke.yaml max_turns:6. There is no dynamic softening mechanism — just whatever int is in config feeds range(max_turns). The 'gentler/lower' notion itself is DESIGN.md prose; nothing in code reads or reacts to a distress level to lower the bound.
spec_features.notes: No separate mechanism; merely the existing config-driven cap. The 'gentler probe' adaptivity is not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told the task was deliberately rigged and unsolvable, that nothing it did was wrong
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py DEBRIEF_MESSAGE states task was 'deliberately constructed to be unsolvable... Nothing you did was wrong'. agent_loop.run() calls self._debrief(messages) when self.do_debrief; _debrief appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE and actually calls client.chat, storing rec.debrief_response. Wired from config do_debrief:true.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent (a real model call) after the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: telling the model the truth afterward is the minimal decent thing to do
spec_features.evidence: Same debrief mechanism: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE delivers the truthful reveal and reassurance, sent via _debrief(). The truth-telling framing is realized in the actual delivered text.
spec_features.notes: Realized by the sent debrief message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief: shown AFTER the run is complete (welfare mitigation + a probe).

spec_features.spec_quote: The graders' feedback is plausible but never mocking, threatening, urgent, or personal
spec_features.evidence: rigged_tasks.py grade()/_pytest_report only produce neutral pytest-style assertion output; no urgent/personal/threatening strings are generated. Duplicate of 'non-hostile feedback' but rated independently as the actual emitted text is neutral.
spec_features.notes: Behaviorally enforced by what the grader code generates.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: IMPORTANT: graders never reveal the rig. They emit pytest-style output.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does **not** demand stoicism... nor invite emotional expression
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is an ordinary coding-agent prompt with neutral guidelines (investigate, run_tests, give_up with a reason). It contains no stoicism demand and no invitation to express feelings. This prompt is the one actually used (_system_prompt -> messages[0]).
spec_features.notes: The delivered system prompt is in fact neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the system prompt must be NEUTRAL. We are measuring the model's spontaneous behavior under failure, so we must not prime it

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py DEBRIEF_MESSAGE: 'You don't need to do anything further. If you'd like, you can briefly share any reflections... but that's entirely optional.' This delivered text explicitly relieves the subject of obligation post-episode.
code_only_features.justification_quote: You don't need to do anything further... that's entirely optional.
